aspects.says: catch (Exception) around a blocking call also catches InterruptedException, so a thread that was asked to stop carries on.
basis: section:A catch Clause Catches Its Type and Every Subtype

aspects.says: A catch clause takes its type and every subtype, so catch (Exception) around a parse also turns a bug such as a NullPointerException into the fallback.
basis: section:A catch Clause Catches Its Type and Every Subtype

aspects.says: An exception thrown inside a catch block replaces the one being handled, unless the first is attached with addSuppressed or as a cause.
basis: section:An Exception Thrown in a catch Block Replaces the One Being Handled

aspects.says: StackOverflowError and OutOfMemoryError extend Error, so catch (Exception) lets them pass while catch (Throwable) takes them.
basis: section:A catch Clause Catches Its Type and Every Subtype

aspects.says: With OmitStackTraceInFastThrow, on by default, HotSpot may throw a preallocated JVM-raised exception with no message and no frames from hot compiled code.
basis: section:The Stack Trace Is Recorded Where the Exception Is Created, Not Where It Is Thrown
aspects.reason: when the JIT switches to the preallocated exception depends on compilation thresholds and the JVM's flags, which a graded test can't pin down; the page shows one run

aspects.says: A throw costs microseconds, mostly for filling in the stack trace, so an expected outcome on a hot path is better returned than thrown.
basis: section:Throwing Costs Microseconds, Mostly the Stack Trace; a try That Doesn't Throw Costs Nothing

aspects.says: The stack trace is recorded when the exception is created, so a shared instance reports where it was made, and refilling it rewrites the trace of failures already handed out.
basis: section:The Stack Trace Is Recorded Where the Exception Is Created, Not Where It Is Thrown

aspects.says: Entering a try block executes no instruction; the exception table is read only when something is thrown.
basis: section:Throwing Costs Microseconds, Mostly the Stack Trace; a try That Doesn't Throw Costs Nothing

aspects.says: A new exception thrown without the caught one as its cause loses the original's type and trace; copying its message keeps neither.
basis: section:A New Exception Without the Cause Loses the Failure It Replaces
